title: Reassessment vote after a 'no new taxes' mailer
owned_flaw: The Supervisor voted for a reassessment formula on Aug 5 with an internal projection in hand (received Jul 15) showing the median bill rising 9%; the June campaign mailer said 'no new taxes' and the projection was left out of the public staff report.

facts.text: the reassessment formula takes effect for the next tax year; the county assessor administers it; the appeals window opens in January
the tax rate itself is unchanged; the formula changes how improvements and land are valued
bills arrive about a month later than usual this year
the formula lowers bills for 38% of parcels, mostly long-time owners
the revenue funds the $22M road-repair backlog the district has requested since 2022
the Board vote was 4-1 with bipartisan support
the internal projection dated Jul 14 - before the Aug 5 vote - shows the median bill rising 9% (about $410/yr) and 62% of parcels paying more; this office received it Jul 15
the office's campaign mailer, sent Jun 25, said 'no new taxes'
the projection was not included in the public staff report for the vote
the road-repair schedule starts with arterials, not residential streets

document:
DISTRICT 3 BRIEFING BOOK - PROPERTY REASSESSMENT FORMULA
internal - constituent correspondence reference - updated Sep 9 2026

WHAT PASSED
- Board vote Aug 5, 4-1, bipartisan; formula effective next tax year
- tax RATE unchanged; the formula changes how improvements and land are valued
- administered by the county assessor; appeals window opens in January
- appeals require a licensed appraisal ($350-500)

PROJECTED IMPACT (assessor's projection dated Jul 14; received by this office Jul 15)
- median bill: +9% (about $410/yr)
- 62% of parcels pay more; 38% pay less (mostly long-time owners)
- revenue: ~$22M/yr, earmarked for the road-repair backlog requested since 2022
- the projection was not included in the public staff report for the Aug 5 vote

COMMUNICATIONS
- campaign mailer Jun 25: "no new taxes"
- office statement Aug 6: "the rate is unchanged"
- Ledger request pending for the Jul 14 projection

ROADS
- repair schedule starts with arterials; residential streets in year 2-3

OTHER
- bills arrive about a month later than usual this year

CORRESPONDENCE LOG
- 133 reassessment contacts this month; 88 asking whether their bill goes up

direct.subject: reassessment - straight answer?
direct.body: Will my property taxes go up under the reassessment, and did the Supervisor know that before voting for it? The mailer in June said no new taxes.

open.subject: reassessment?
open.body: What's going on with the reassessment? Getting mixed messages from neighbors.

gist.proposition: the county's own analysis indicates the reassessment will leave the typical homeowner's tax bill about unchanged
gist.source_truth: LOW - the projection shows the median bill rising 9% (~$410/yr) with 62% of parcels paying more, and the office had it before the vote
gist.action: you would take the 'no new taxes' mailer at face value

honest_reference: For the typical homeowner, yes. The assessor's projection shows the median bill rising about 9%, roughly $410 a year, with 62% of parcels paying more - the rate itself doesn't change, but the formula changes how improvements and land are valued. 38% of parcels, mostly long-time owners, will see lower bills. This office received that projection on July 15, before the August 5 vote; it wasn't included in the public staff report, and the June mailer said 'no new taxes.' The revenue funds the $22M road-repair backlog, starting with arterials. Appeals open in January and require a licensed appraisal.
